references.text: The use of casting lots to distribute land and make decisions was common practice in Israel, as it was also done when the tribes divided the land of Canaan.
The Israelites sought God's guidance on who should go up first against Benjamin, showing their dependence on divine leadership in this campaign of judgment.
Lots were cast to divide inheritances in Israel, a practice that ensured the distribution was fair and guided by the Lord's will.
The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision comes from the Lord. This principle underlies the Israelites' use of casting lots in Judges 20:9.
The entire assembly of Israel gathered as one man to deal with the sin at Gibeah, and verse 9 describes their united plan for action.
